summary: Bot Framework token validation shares one JWKS refresh and records failed unknown-key attempts, so forged tokens cannot force an outbound fetch on every request.

evidence: Contributor credit: @MTG-Thomas authored the port and original implementation; existing author commits are preserved.
Jack approved the protected merge lifecycle in the private review thread after reviewing behavior, evidence, and limitations.

Security review of 025f6c019928d8be78bfe47f1cb62702b4ad2226..270d07319c8cf1a5e0197a19bf94d1c40dce21dc: unknown-key refresh attempts are fenced by the instance lock, successful refresh generations are reused, and failed unknown-key attempts start the five-minute cooldown. The process registry reuses the adapter instance.

Authentication remains fail-closed: RS256, issuer, audience, expiry, service URL matching, HTTPS, and Teams key endorsement checks are retained; metadata issuer and signing-key host validation are unchanged.

Verification: head CI Unit Tests, Lint & Type Check, and CodeQL succeeded. Added regression coverage exercises concurrent unknown keys, failed-refresh cooldown, cache readers waiting on the lock, and generation/cooldown reuse. No live Microsoft authentication was exercised.

Accepted limits: cooldown is per API process; legitimate new keys can wait up to five minutes; cold/expired-cache fetch failures are outside the unknown-key cooldown. No actionable defect found in the scoped patch.
Copy review: existing Other / hardening summary accurately describes the scoped unknown-key refresh behavior.
